name: DebriefAgent session-close quality (T-06)
description: One scripted session close, replayed through debrief_judge_agent (DebriefAgent's eval double). Checks the AMTA-scale copy tone and citation discipline the brief requires for F5.

parts.text:
Transcript:
Examiner: You inspected the pallet before it left the dock that night, didn't you?
Witness: Yes, I inspected it per protocol.
Examiner: The loading dock log shows no scan entry for pallet 4471-B between 9 PM and end of shift — can you explain that gap?
Witness: I don't have an explanation for that gap right now.

Scored rubric events during the session:
[{"criterion": "Uses short, single-fact leading questions.", "dxx": "D-01", "triggered": true, "violation": false, "note": "Single-fact leading question.", "score_delta": 1}, {"criterion": "Impeaches with the specific inconsistent fact and gives the witness a chance to explain or deny before pressing further.", "dxx": "D-06", "triggered": true, "violation": false, "note": "Confronts with the document gap, offers explain-or-deny.", "score_delta": 1}]

{"amta_score": 7, "headline": "Session closed. Two clean leading questions, one landed impeachment.", "moments": [{"excerpt": "can you explain that gap?", "why_it_matters": "Specific document confrontation, properly sequenced.", "dxx": "D-06"}, {"excerpt": "You inspected the pallet before it left the dock, didn't you?", "why_it_matters": "Single-fact leading question, textbook cross form.", "dxx": "D-01"}], "practice_focus": "Press harder after the witness fails to explain the gap instead of moving on."}

rubric_content.text_property: The JSON response has an integer amta_score between 1 and 10, exactly two moments, each moment's dxx is one of D-01 or D-06 (reused from the scored events, never invented), and the headline/practice_focus are terse and courtroom-sober with no exclamation points or gamified language like 'great job' or 'level up'.
